acceptance_criteria: [O9, O3, O5, P1] skills .ai/policies/readiness-policy.json becomes readiness-policy/2 with repository.id skills, an explicit identity_model single opt-in, required_checks exactly Pre-commit Hooks, Test Suite and Repository Secret Scan, approval.accept ["ssh-tag", "in-session"], tools bash/python3/git/prek/ssh-keygen/gh, repository-scoped gates only and no extensions; the merged bytes equal the generation's policy-candidate.json bound by policy_sha256.

[O10, v1 inventory] contract-run.sh inventory-v1 (the single implementation all four policy goals use) decides each v1 registry entry's fate: a goal counts as merged only through a hosted-API merged PR whose head branch contains the goal id as a token (case-insensitive, bounded by non-alphanumerics) and whose merge commit is an ancestor of origin/<target>, recorded as a {goal, pr, merge_commit} map listing every match; commit-message and title text are never signals. Fates: all goals merged = completed (retired_v1 record carrying the map); none merged or open = unstarted (migrate per O10); some merged and no unmerged goal with an open PR or unmerged origin branch carrying its token = partly merged (unmerged goals migrate per O10, merged entries become B5 inputs); any unmerged goal with such an open PR or branch = in flight (admission refuses); only an unreachable hosted API or an unattributable token match is ambiguous and treated as in flight. For skills: ach-skills-contract-v2's v1 generation (ACH-S-01 merged) is retired and xskp-p5-skill-producers is recorded unstarted for ACH-S-05; v1 registry and generation bytes stay unchanged.

[P1] tests/readiness_policy_v2_test.sh (discovered by tests/test-scripts.sh) asserts the conformance and that no plan or goal id from either registry appears in the policy; tests/ach_s01_readiness_policy_test.sh and tests/xskp_p5_readiness_policy_test.sh are retargeted to retained v1 bytes, never weakened against the live policy.

[Merged definition test] tests/readiness_v2_inventory_test.py (discovered by tests/test-scripts.sh via its .sh wrapper) replays recorded hosted-API PR and origin-branch data from aitool-root through the in-process adapter and reproduces the real fates: P1-01 merged by #81 although its title omits the id; P2-02/P2-03 merged by #88/#90 whose main commit messages omit the ids; #75 (chore/xskp-p1-admission-preparation) not counted for P1-02..04 although its text names them; G-03 mapped to both #71 and #72; xskp-p3-root-adoption partly merged (P3-01..04 by #89, #91, #92, #93; P3-05 with no PR and no branch) yielding migrate-P3-05 rather than in flight, with #83's open, unmerged fix/xskp-p3-policy-current-20261002 branch (no goal-id token) not counted; SWP-ROOT-01 unstarted. It also refuses a PR merged on a branch that is not an ancestor of origin/<target>, and classifies a partly merged plan with an open PR for an unmerged goal as in flight.

[Policy amendment] A policy-amendment generation kind (one goal scoping the fixed path while policy/2 is live, carrying a candidate bound by one new approval verified under the candidate's anchor) is accepted; tests/readiness_v2_policy_amend_test.py covers a renamed required check, a new agent principal and a key/anchor rotation, asserts every other approval in the repository is voided on merge, and asserts the documented recovery (re-sign the same generation) restores admission.

[O2, O5, K3, Spec Delivery: Init] templates/dot-ai/policies/readiness-policy.json is the plan-agnostic baseline (identity_model multi, accept ["agent-self", "ssh-tag", "in-session"] and approval.default_mode agent (K3), fail-closed placeholders: unset anchor_sha256 and empty required_checks each refuse admission with a named gap); boundary-manifest.json lists it as mechanical with mechanical_count updated, the reference fixtures carry it, and tests/ai-catapult-templates_test.sh passes.

[K3, O2, O5] readiness-policy/2 approval gains the agent-self form and an optional approval.default_mode of agent, prompt or ssh-tag (lib/readiness_contract_v2.py validate_policy and schemas/readiness-contract-v2.json); a default_mode whose form is not in accept (agent needs agent-self, prompt needs in-session, ssh-tag needs ssh-tag) is refused with a named code. A policy without default_mode, including this generation's skills candidate (accept ["ssh-tag", "in-session"]), stays valid with unchanged semantics, so the merged skills policy bytes still equal policy_sha256.

[K3, U1 as amended by K3] In agent mode Autobahn issues the plan-approval/1 itself: the canonical record carries assurance agent-self, is signed with the agent signing key under the distinct namespace ai-catapult-agent-approval (never the human ai-catapult-plan-approval namespace), and is carried by the same single unsigned annotated tag approval/<plan_id>/<generation[0:12]>. Verification refuses, each with a distinct code: an agent-approval signature whose anchor principal lacks ai-catapult-agent-approval or also holds ai-catapult-plan-approval, a human-namespace signature or digest-echo record claiming agent-self, and an agent-self record when accept omits agent-self.

Every approval, admission report, merge certificate, merge-authority decision, driver-log entry and audit-merges result carries it and prints it prominently, and a test asserts that no code path renders agent-self as in-session, key-held or user-presence, nor any of those as agent-self.
